text:
maria_ops: Heads-up — since the overnight driver roll (525 -> 550 candidate) we've got ~120 nodes stuck in provisioning: most are failing DKMS module build during boot and dropping to emergency shell. Happening across us-west2 and eu-central, but not ap-southeast. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam_infra: Saw noise in autoscaler — new spot nodes keep failing init, then scale-down churn. Got a few journal snippets: 

kevin_runtime: paste the logs?

maria_ops: here's one from a failed boot (short):

"""
Nov 10 03:12:44 ip-10-10-2-45 kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
Nov 10 03:12:44 ip-10-10-2-45 dkms: ERROR: Cannot create module tree: /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/550.12/build
Nov 10 03:12:44 ip-10-10-2-45 dkms: Kernel preparation unnecessary for this kernel.
Nov 10 03:12:44 ip-10-10-2-45 dkms: Building module:
Nov 10 03:12:44 ip-10-10-2-45 make[1]: *** No rule to make target '/lib/modules/5.15.0-1029-aws/build'.  Stop.
Nov 10 03:12:44 ip-10-10-2-45 systemd[1]: Started /usr/bin/dkms build for nvidia-550.
Nov 10 03:12:45 ip-10-10-2-45 systemd[1]: nvidia-dkms.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=2/INVALIDARGUMENT
"""

lina_sre: Interesting: the kernel headers package on those AMIs is the older 5.15 variant, but our driver package expects the 5.18 build symlink. Could be the AMI bake got mixed with a previous kernel. Also seeing: module signature key has rotated in the company RPM repo yesterday (key id 0xABCD1234).

sam_infra: Wait, we rotated the package signing key yesterday for the driver RPM? That would cause "module verification failed" only if secureboot or module_signature verification is enabled, right? Most of our fleet has module signature checks OFF.

kevin_runtime: We ship drivers as signed RPMs and also provide dkms fallback for kernel mismatches. Two failure modes here: (1) DKMS build failing because /lib/modules/*/build is missing (kernel-devel not present on AMI), (2) module signature mismatch when the kernel enforces signed modules. Could be a combination on spot nodes that use a different AMI family.

maria_ops: Confirmed: the failing spot pools are using an older base AMI (custom-ubuntu-5.15-2024-10-01) that doesn't include kernel-devel package and has secureboot flag toggled in the image metadata. Non-spot (reserved) pools use the new AMI (5.18).

lina_sre: Two attack vectors to mitigate quickly:
- Block the rollout of 550 to pools using older AMIs (add a provisioning gate).
- Publish a hotfix: an unsigned driver fallback package that avoids DKMS attempt when kernel-devel missing, or include kernel-devel in AMI.

sam_infra: For immediate fix I rolled back the driver-CI promotion for the 550 rpm to the staging repo for those pools and queued a canary with 525 on a small subset. Deploy-bot: rolled back tag "driver-550" in staging for eu-central and us-west2?

deploy-bot: rollback action queued: driver-550 -> staging (eu-central, us-west2). ETA ~6m.

kevin_runtime: We should also add a pre-provision hook to our cluster-provisioner that validates /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build exists and kernel package matches driver expectations. Quick check snippet: 

"""bash
if [ ! -d /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build ]; then echo 'missing-headers'; exit 1; fi
"""

maria_ops: Agreed. Also need to update our docs and AMI bake to pin kernel-devel and make sure module-signing key is installed so signed modules load. For the signed-key rotation: the new public key wasn't distributed to a subset of images. That's why some nodes are tainting the kernel.

lina_sre: Action items:
- sam: finish rollback and pause driver promotion pipelines for spot pools (in progress)
- kevin: add pre-provision check and a short-lived daemonset that reports kernel/header mismatch counts
- maria: coordinate AMI bake and push updated images with kernel-devel + new key
- ops: run a one-off re-provision (or manual rebuild) for ~120 affected nodes once images ready

sam_infra: I'll also add a temporary autoscaler filter to avoid launching spot in those subnets until we confirm fixes.

maria_ops: Thanks. One follow-up: can we pull a list of affected hostnames? I'm capturing instance IDs from cloudwatch; will dump to #incidents if anyone wants to sweep. :mag:

kevin_runtime: I'll prepare a tiny script to correlate instance-id -> AMI -> kernel version and upload it.

lina_sre: Good postmortem candidate: signed-key rotation validation gap + AMI drift. Keep notes here and we'll escalate to change approval for key rotations. :white_check_mark:

maria_ops: OK logging this as a long-lived ticket. Will post updates in this thread. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
